sources.title: Operating Systems: Three Easy Pieces
sources.relevance: Provides the operating-system abstraction, virtualization, process, protection, and scheduling scope.
sources.evidence_used: Chapter concepts and end-of-chapter framing informed original bilingual diagnostic prompts.
sources.transfer_limits: Atomic text questions omit hands-on systems behavior and remain pending expert review.

sources.title: OSTEP: Interlude Process API
sources.authority: Official chapter PDF from the textbook authors.
sources.relevance: Covers fork, exec, wait, process creation, and the Unix shell interface.
sources.evidence_used: API semantics and boundary cases informed original prediction and explanation prompts.
sources.transfer_limits: Prompts test conceptual behavior, not exact platform-specific API details or coding skill.

sources.title: OSTEP: Mechanism Limited Direct Execution
sources.authority: Official chapter PDF from the textbook authors.
sources.relevance: Covers privilege modes, traps, controlled kernel entry, timer interrupts, and context switches.
sources.evidence_used: Mechanism sequences and failure cases informed original atomic security and control questions.
sources.transfer_limits: Architecture-specific details are intentionally abstracted; expert review must confirm acceptable generalization.

sources.title: OSTEP CPU Scheduling Chapters
sources.relevance: Covers turnaround and response metrics, FIFO, SJF/STCF, and MLFQ.
sources.evidence_used: Scheduling assumptions and small metric calculations informed original scenario questions.
sources.transfer_limits: Toy schedules simplify real workloads and do not establish external validity.

sources.title: OSTEP Official Homework Catalog
sources.authority: Official homework catalog maintained by the textbook authors.
sources.relevance: Confirms simulator-backed practice for processes, scheduling, MLFQ, and virtualization mechanisms.
sources.evidence_used: Used to audit which concepts support concise state-prediction questions; no prompt was copied.
sources.transfer_limits: The JSON bank does not reproduce simulator traces and therefore tests a narrower skill.
